article_title: Space: The Misguided Promise of Privatization
news_headline: SpaceX's post-IPO plunge sets tense backdrop for first earnings report
post_text:
SpaceX went public on June 12 at a $1.5 trillion valuation. Since then, the stock has shed more than $500 billion in market cap, falling over 50% from its intraday high. Its first earnings report as a public company, released August 4, showed a net loss of $541 million, with Starlink's average revenue per user down roughly a third from its 2023 level. Not since Facebook's 2012 debut has a tech IPO produced this kind of early destruction.

The drop exposes a familiar problem: retail investors priced SpaceX on the promise of a space economy that hasn't arrived yet, while the actual business runs deep losses in its launch and AI units subsidized by a Starlink business under competitive pressure.

A piece we published earlier this year argued exactly this, that the commercialization of space rests on government foundations and subsidized ambition far more than the privatization narrative admits. SpaceX's stumble from a $2.6 trillion peak to below its IPO price is the clearest data point yet. Read the full argument on our website.
